title.topic:
The Children of Israel—
Praising, then Complaining
title.point: We need to praise and thank God and not complain — even when things get hard, God is always faithful to care for us!

lastWeekReview.title: The Exodus from Egypt—Crossing the Red Sea
bullets: God Led the Way! He went before His people in a PILLAR OF CLOUD by day and PILLAR OF FIRE by night.
Pharaoh changed his mind and sent his army to chase them!
The Israelites were trapped — sea in front, army behind!
Moses said: 'Do not be afraid! Stand still and see!'
God parted the Red Sea — the water stood like WALLS on each side!
Every Israelite crossed safely on DRY ground. Not one Egyptian was left!
lastWeekReview.discussion: 📖  Did anyone face something scary or impossible-looking this week? How did you trust God through it? Remember — even when things look impossible, God always makes a way!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: "Trust in Jehovah with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding." — Proverbs 3:5

kidsContent.text: After God parted the Red Sea and saved all the Israelites, they were SO happy! They were filled with gratitude and amazement at what God had done.
So what did they do? They PRAISED God by singing! Moses and all the people sang a song: 'I will sing to Jehovah, for He has triumphed gloriously! The horse and its rider He has cast into the sea!'
Then Miriam, Moses' sister, took a tambourine, and all the women danced and sang with her! Singing is a wonderful way to praise God and show Him how thankful we are.
What does it mean to praise? It means words of approval and admiration — and worshipping and thanking God! When your parents say 'PRAISE THE LORD!' they are thanking God!
🌟 Praising God makes us HAPPY! It also makes God happy! Singing to God is one of the best things we can do!

image.caption: Miriam and the women praise God with singing and dancing

kidsContent.text: But the praising didn't last very long. Right after all the singing and celebration, the Israelites started to COMPLAIN!
First they complained there was no water. Then they found water at a place called Marah — but it was BITTER! They grumbled: 'What are we going to drink?!'
What a short memory! God had just done the most AMAZING miracle — parting the whole Red Sea! And now they were already complaining? Aren't we all like that sometimes?
Moses cried out to God, and God showed him a special tree. When Moses threw the tree into the bitter water, it became SWEET! Once again, the faithful God came through for His people.
A complainer is always miserable, grumbling and whining. But a person who praises is full of joy! Which one do you want to be?
🌟 No matter how much we complain, God still cares for us — but let's choose to be praisers, not complainers!

image.caption: The Israelites complain about the bitter water at Marah

lesson.practicePoint: This week, whenever you feel like complaining about something, STOP and find something to praise God for instead! Count how many times you turn a complaint into praise, and share your experience next week.

memoryVerse.text: I will praise You… / Your works are wonderful, / And my soul knows it well.
memoryVerse.application: The Israelites praised God after He parted the Red Sea — His works truly ARE wonderful! When we remember all the amazing things God has done for us, our response should be praise, not complaining. Our soul can know how wonderful He is!

parts.text: Materials: Whiteboard/paper, markers, two boxes labeled 'PRAISE' and 'COMPLAIN'
Round 1 — Sort It Out: Read different statements. Kids decide if it's a praise or complaint and put it in the right box. E.g., 'It's raining again!' (complain) vs. 'Thank God for water!' (praise)
Round 2 — Flip It: Take each complaint card and challenge kids to 'flip' it into a praise! E.g., 'This food is boring' → 'Thank God we have food to eat!'
Round 3 — Praise Relay: Two teams. Each team writes as many praises as they can in 2 minutes. The team with the most praises wins!
Discussion: Was it hard to flip complaints into praises? Which felt better — complaining or praising?
📖 Connection: The Israelites complained right after God did something amazing. We want to be praisers — people who remember what God has done and thank Him!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: The shore of the Red Sea. The Israelites have just crossed safely. They are overjoyed!
God had just done the most AMAZING miracle — parting the Red Sea and saving all His people! The Israelites were so happy, they burst into song!
I will sing to Jehovah, for He has triumphed gloriously! The horse and its rider He has cast into the sea!
Everyone, grab your tambourines! Let's sing and dance to praise our God!
Everyone sings and dances joyfully! Miriam leads the women with tambourines.
Praise the Lord! He saved us! He is SO faithful!
But the praising didn't last very long. After three days of walking in the wilderness, they found water — but it was BITTER!
The Israelites taste the water and make disgusted faces.
Blech! This water is TERRIBLE! I can't drink this!
Moses, what are we supposed to drink?! Did you bring us out here to die of thirst?!
Wait — didn't God just part an entire SEA for them? And now they're complaining about water? How quickly they forgot!
Lord, what should I do? The people are so unhappy!
Moses, do you see that tree? Throw it into the water.
Moses throws the tree into the bitter water. The Israelites taste it again.
Wait — it's SWEET now! The water is sweet! God did it again!
No matter how much we complain, God still cares for us — but let's choose to be PRAISERS, not complainers! Praising makes us happy, and it makes God happy too!

description.text: Setup: Play upbeat praise music. Kids dance and move around the gym freely.
When the music stops, the leader calls out a scenario: 'You can't find your favorite toy!' Kids must shout a PRAISE instead of a complaint.
If you complain or can't think of a praise in 5 seconds, you do 3 jumping jacks before rejoining.
Scenarios: 'Your sibling took your snack', 'It's raining on your field day', 'You have to clean your room', 'Your tablet died!'
📖 Connection: Just like the Israelites needed to choose praising over complaining, we practice turning complaints into praise!
Materials: Bluetooth speaker, praise music playlist, scenario cards
Setup: Two teams. Each has a bucket of 'bitter water' (crumpled paper balls) at one end and an empty 'sweet water' bucket at the other.
Rules: Runners carry one paper ball at a time from 'bitter' to 'sweet' bucket. But they must say something they're thankful for before dropping the ball in!
If they can't think of a praise, they must run back and try again!
First team to turn all their 'bitter water' into 'sweet water' wins!
📖 Connection: God turned the bitter water at Marah sweet — and when we praise instead of complain, God turns our bitter situations sweet too!
Materials: Two sets of buckets, crumpled paper balls, cones

description.text: Kids explore the outdoor area looking for things to praise God for! Each kid or team gets a 'Praise Card' with categories.
Categories: Something beautiful, something that makes a sound, something alive, something that keeps you safe, something you can smell.
For each item found, kids write a one-sentence praise. E.g., 'Thank You God for this flower — it shows Your creativity!'
Twist: Include one 'hard' category — 'Find something you'd normally complain about and turn it into a praise!'
Materials: Printed Praise Cards, pencils, clipboards

outdoor.tip: 🎵 Singing praise songs together while walking outdoors is a great way to connect this lesson! Encourage kids to notice God's creation and say 'Thank You!' instead of complaining about the weather, bugs, etc.
